scope: specialize group-homomorphism kernel to abelian groups
paraphrase: For an abelian-group homomorphism f:A→B, its kernel is the subgroup {a∈A:f(a)=0_B}, with its canonical inclusion into A.
necessary_caveat: ProofWiki gives ordinary group kernel; specializing to abelian groups changes multiplicative e_B to additive 0_B and agrees with categorical kernel in Ab. The source does not itself define cokernels or exact sequences.

paraphrase: A kernel of a morphism f:x→y is an arrow i:k→x with fi=0 and universal among arrows j:z→x killed by f, uniquely factoring through i.
necessary_caveat: Exists only if the particular morphism admits a kernel. The kernel as a morphism/object universal property is not literally the same data as the concrete subset of elements used in Ab.

paraphrase: A cokernel of f:x→y is an arrow p:y→c with pf=0 that is universal among arrows q:y→z with qf=0, each factoring uniquely through p.
necessary_caveat: In Ab this can be represented by y/im f with the quotient map, but in a general preadditive category cokernels need not exist and are unique only up to unique isomorphism.

scope: exactness for a complex in an abelian category
paraphrase: A complex has zero composites of consecutive morphisms. At an interior object Y of X→Y→Z it is exact when im(X→Y)=ker(Y→Z). A short exact sequence is 0→A→B→C→0.
necessary_caveat: For abelian groups the categorical im/ker specializes to subgroup image and subgroup kernel, but a general additive category need not be abelian and the concept of exactness cannot be exported there without hypotheses.
